newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon as institutions buy.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon as institutions buy.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were up solidly at midday on Monday with institutions buying companies which have a heavy weighting in the index, including Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co, brokers said.
The B share index rose 1.754 points or 1.99 percent to 89.852 points on volume of 12.581 million shares worth $8.462 million, compared with $8.7 million on Friday.
Brokers said domestic institutions were still the main force in the market, but some overseas capital was also seen entering the market on expectations of further gains by blue chips.
"Overseas institutions were seen building positions in companies with good results and prospects," said one broker.

"The index will rise further in the short term on good sentiment," another broker said. "But some companies are still expected to post poor 1996 results, which may have a negative impact on the market."
Of 43 B shares, 30 traded, with 18 up, four flat and eight down.
Shanghai Lujiazui was the most actively traded share as well as the top performer on institutional buying, jumping $0.100 or 7.39 percent to $1.452 on volume of 1.7 million shares.
Huangshan Tourism Development also gained on institutional buying, ending the morning up $0.046 or 5.82 percent at $0.836 on volume of 194,000 shares.
Shanghai's A share index rose in active trading, but the market is likely to correct in the short term due to an uncertain outlook, brokers said.
The A index gained 5.195 points or 0.36 percent to 1,432.167 points on volume of 365.1 million shares worth 5.3 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index jumped 117.952 points or 3.11 percent to 3,911.766 points.
Chongqing Wanli Storage Battery was the star A share on speculative buying, surging 0.95 yuan or 10.05 percent to 10.40 yuan on volume of 3.1 million shares.
